Theme

# Philosophy quotes about morality

Morality in philosophy concerns right and wrong, obligation, and the standards by which we judge persons and acts.

34 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Moral philosophy asks whether morality is objective, how reasons bind us, and how character, rules, and consequences relate. Traditions differ on whether duty, virtue, or outcomes come first.

## In the history of philosophy

From Confucian and Greek virtue vocabularies to Kantian duty, utilitarianism, and critiques of moral ideology, the theme remains central to public life.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) , [Iris Murdoch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/iris-murdoch) , [Bhagavad Gita](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bhagavad-gita) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is morality in philosophy?

It is the domain of norms about right action, good character, and what we owe one another—studied systematically in ethics.

### How is morality different from ethics?

In everyday speech they overlap; academically, ethics often names the philosophical study of moral practices and concepts.
